title: Mobile Development
commonInfo:
## Mobile Development Fundamentals

### Responsive Design & Adaptive Layout

- Design for variable screen sizes, pixel densities, and aspect ratios — **NEVER** assume a fixed viewport.
- Respect platform safe areas (notches, status bars, navigation bars) — use framework-provided safe area wrappers.
- Support both portrait and landscape orientations unless explicitly scoped to one.
- Use relative sizing and flexible layouts instead of hardcoded pixel dimensions.

### Offline-First & Data Persistence

- Assume network connectivity is unreliable — cache critical data locally and sync when connection is restored.
- Implement optimistic UI updates for user actions — confirm with server asynchronously.
- **NEVER** block the UI thread with synchronous network calls or heavy I/O operations.
- Persist user session state to survive app restarts and process termination.

### Platform Guidelines

- Follow **Material Design** guidelines for Android and **Human Interface Guidelines** for iOS.
- Use platform-adaptive components that respect native user expectations (navigation patterns, gestures, typography).
- **NEVER** mix platform idioms — a bottom tab bar on Android and a hamburger menu on iOS is acceptable; the reverse is not.

### App Lifecycle & Background Handling

- Handle foreground/background transitions gracefully — pause timers, close connections, save draft state.
- Release expensive resources (camera, GPS, audio) when the app moves to background.
- Implement state restoration so users return to exactly where they left off.

### Permissions & Privacy

- Request permissions lazily at the point of use — **NEVER** request all permissions at app launch.
- Provide clear, user-facing explanations for why each permission is needed before the system dialog appears.
- Gracefully degrade functionality when permissions are denied — **NEVER** crash or show blank screens.

### Accessibility

- Provide semantic labels for all interactive and informational elements for screen readers (VoiceOver, TalkBack).
- Ensure minimum touch target sizes of 48x48dp for all interactive elements.
- Support dynamic text scaling — **NEVER** use fixed font sizes that ignore user accessibility settings.
- Maintain sufficient color contrast ratios (WCAG AA minimum: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text).
